relevance_note: Three family members (proband, his sister, his daughter) with chronic urticaria and angioedema carry a heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense VUS: "each carry the c.65G>A (p.R22Q) variant inTNFAIP3"; none is diagnosed with HA20.
method_note: Manual reading of the full text (no tables in the paper); a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans and fields. Labels are verbatim: 'the proband', 'his sister', 'his daughter', 'his mother'. The mother was sequenced, tested negative for the TNFAIP3 variant and carries the GJB2 variant, so she has a row but no TNFAIP3 variant row. The father (mentioned only as deceased) and other sisters (implied by 'one of the proband's sisters') have no clinical or genetic information and no rows; the pedigree (Figure 1) is not in the text. Contradictions/inconsistencies: Methods say reads were aligned to GRCh37/hg19 but Results give GRCh38 coordinates; the GJB2 variant is printed as c.35del (Results) and c.35delG (Conclusion), recorded as the Results string for both carriers; the Introduction ('did not detect any causative variants in known disease genes') and Limitations ('no other disease-associated variants') sit uneasily with the pathogenic GJB2 variant reported in Results (attributed to hearing loss); the TNFAIP3 protein change is printed both as p.(Arg22Gln) and p.R22Q. Functional evidence is in silico only (prediction tools and molecular modeling); no wet-lab assay. Inheritance left 'not reported' for all carriers (mother negative, father deceased; daughter's origin not stated). Judgement calls: checklist 'skin lesions' marked observed from urticaria/hives; 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' observed from the elevated anti-IgE receptor antibody; 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' excluded from a normal CBC with differential; 'recurrent fever' observed from attacks every two weeks involving fever; the mother's chronic urticaria and angioedema excluded from 'unaffected'. Age at onset 'early 30s' not converted to ISO 8601.
